title: Danny Trejo Clarifies ‘Pawn Shop’ Role: “I’m Pro‑Immigrant, Not Pro‑ICE” – Variety Exclusive
body:
Danny Trejo has publicly addressed the controversy surrounding his involvement in the Daily Wire’s upcoming thriller “Pawn Shop,” insisting that his participation does not equate to an endorsement of the network’s hard‑line immigration stance. The Mexican‑American actor, best known for his iconic roles in “Machete” and “From Dusk Till Dawn,” issued a statement on social media after a wave of criticism from activists and fans who accused him of aligning with an anti‑immigrant agenda promoted by the right‑leaning outlet.

In the post, Trejo emphasized his personal identity and lifelong advocacy for immigrant rights, writing, “I am a proud Mexican who has always stood with my community. I am not pro‑ICE; I am pro‑immigrant.” He clarified that his decision to work on the film was driven by the script’s focus on a gritty crime story, not by any political messaging. “The movie is about a pawn shop owner caught in a dangerous underworld, nothing more,” he added. The actor’s remarks aim to separate his artistic choices from the political climate that surrounds the Daily Wire’s expanding foray into entertainment.

The backlash began when “Pawn Shop,” produced by Ben Shapiro’s The Daily Wire, was announced in early June. The network, known for its conservative commentary, has recently launched a film division that has drawn scrutiny for its perceived ideological bent. Critics pointed to the film’s premise—a narrative involving illegal immigration, border enforcement, and a criminal enterprise—as a potential vehicle for pro‑ICE sentiment. Social‑media users, advocacy groups, and some members of the Hollywood community called for Trejo to withdraw, arguing that his involvement could lend credibility to a platform they view as hostile to immigrant communities.

Trejo’s response reflects a broader tension within the entertainment industry, where actors increasingly face pressure to align their careers with their personal political beliefs. In recent years, several high‑profile performers have been called out for working with studios or producers accused of promoting divisive policies. The actor’s decision to address the issue directly, rather than remain silent, underscores a growing expectation that public figures articulate their stance on contentious matters, especially when their heritage or personal history is implicated.

Industry analysts suggest that the controversy may have mixed implications for the film’s reception. On one hand, the publicity generated by the dispute could boost curiosity and drive viewership among both supporters and detractors of the Daily Wire’s messaging. On the other hand, the negative press may alienate segments of the audience who view the film as a propaganda piece, potentially limiting its box‑office prospects or streaming numbers. Moreover, Trejo’s clarification could mitigate some of the backlash, allowing the film to be judged on its cinematic merits rather than its perceived political agenda.

As “Pawn Shop” approaches its release later this year, the conversation surrounding Trejo’s involvement is likely to continue. The actor’s statement may set a precedent for how other performers navigate collaborations with politically charged production houses. Whether the film succeeds in separating its narrative from the ideological leanings of its backers remains to be seen, but the episode highlights the increasingly porous boundary between entertainment and politics in an era of heightened cultural scrutiny.
